key_insight: For D-gun sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr coatings on DSS 2205, a 190 mm spray distance produced the densest coating and the best corrosion resistance in 1 M H2SO4.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing spray distance is a practical lever to improve coating compactness and acid-corrosion protection for stainless steel parts used in harsh industrial environments.
method: D-gun sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr onto DSS 2205 at 170, 180, and 190 mm.
Characterized surface/microstructure with SEM and porosity measurements.
Evaluated corrosion behavior in 1 M H2SO4 using OCP, EIS, and potentiodynamic polarization.
evidence_signal: Porosity decreased from 2.84% at 170 mm to 1.38% at 190 mm, and the 190 mm coating showed the lowest corrosion rate (0.113 mmpy) versus 2.60 mmpy for uncoated DSS 2205.
watch_item: The optimum distance is specific to this powder, substrate, and acidic test condition, so transfer to other process windows or service environments should be validated experimentally.
paper_title: Effect of spray distance in D-gun sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr coatings on DSS 2205 in acidic environments
